email.body1:
Nate, saw Teamworks raise $235M and snap up Sportlogiq and PFF Enterprise to build out the AI platform.

A raise plus back-to-back acquisitions usually opens more in-market teams and programs than sales can personally cover before momentum fades, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Teamworks off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Nate, quick follow-up for Teamworks.

Post-raise and post-acquisition, expectations on pipeline usually jump faster than headcount can. Most teams do not actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Teamworks needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Nate, last bit of proof for Teamworks.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Teamworks' reply rate likely compares to other growth-stage startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?

Nate, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.
